processes.title: Sales Inquiry
processes.memory_hook: Customer asks. We qualify before we promise.
processes.business_intent: Capture an early customer request before a formal quotation or order exists, preserving requirements and follow-on traceability without creating a fulfillment commitment.

control_plane.why: define how long the request remains commercially relevant
control what is copied into quotation or order
separate active opportunities from closed requests

data_hinges.changes: what later quotation or order must solve
partner, pricing and sales-area context for follow-on documents

impact_summary: No inventory or accounting movement occurs; the value is preserving demand context before a formal commercial promise is made.
constraints: Do not turn every vague customer conversation into ERP master data or a sales document.
CRM/Sales Cloud may own opportunity qualification while S/4HANA owns the transactional inquiry.
lead_questions: Which information belongs in CRM versus S/4?
When should an inquiry become a quotation?
What must be copied and what should be redetermined later?

processes.title: Sales with One-Time Customer
processes.memory_hook: Sell once without pretending the buyer deserves a permanent master record.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Order Entry with One-Time Customer

processes.business_intent: Run a normal sales transaction for an occasional buyer while entering transaction-specific address and partner information instead of maintaining a dedicated customer master for every one-off sale.

control_plane.why: provides the reusable account shell
stores the actual buyer details for this transaction
ensures the temporary partner context still produces valid billing and FI documents

data_hinges.changes: tax determination and legal invoice data

impact_summary: The fulfillment process remains ordinary, but master-data governance moves from a permanent customer record into the transaction.
constraints: Not suitable when repeated business, credit history, contracts, rebates or customer-specific master data are expected.
Duplicate use can become a data-quality loophole if users avoid proper customer onboarding.
lead_questions: When does a one-time buyer become a real customer master?
Which controls prevent duplicate or fraudulent one-time addresses?
How do credit, tax and sanctions checks work for transient partner data?

processes.title: Free Goods Processing
processes.memory_hook: The order has value, but part of the quantity is deliberately free.
processes.business_intent: Grant bonus quantities according to commercial rules while keeping the paid and free quantities explicit in order, delivery and pricing behavior.

control_plane.why: decides eligibility, minimum quantity and bonus quantity
decides whether free quantity is inside or added on top of ordered quantity
keeps bonus items free while preserving logistics

data_hinges.changes: total delivered quantity and commercial interpretation

impact_summary: Revenue and delivered quantity no longer move one-to-one; logistics must still execute the free quantity correctly.
constraints: Free goods are different from a full free-of-charge order and from a complaint replacement.
Partial delivery and quantity changes can recalculate or redistribute the free quantity.
lead_questions: Is the bonus inside the ordered quantity or additional?
What happens when the customer changes quantity after determination?
How should free quantity affect margin and promotion analytics?

processes.title: Returnables Processing
processes.memory_hook: We sell the goods; the packaging is expected to come back.
processes.business_intent: Track reusable packaging or containers delivered to customers while retaining ownership and expecting later return or settlement.

control_plane.why: separates reusable asset-like packaging from the sold product
tracks company-owned returnables located at the customer
decides whether packaging comes back or is commercially settled

impact_summary: Location changes without immediate ownership transfer, similar to consignment logic but for reusable packaging rather than saleable customer stock.
constraints: Requires discipline around customer stock reconciliation; otherwise pallets and containers quietly become a permanent donation program.
Returnables and consignment solve different business objects even though both use customer-located special stock concepts.
lead_questions: Who owns the packaging at each step?
How is overdue returnable stock reconciled or charged?
Can warehouse execution create returnables delivery without a new sales order?

processes.title: Collective Billing and Invoice Lists
processes.memory_hook: Fulfill many times; present the commercial result in fewer documents.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Order Processing with Invoice List and Collective Billing

processes.business_intent: Consolidate multiple billable references into collective billing documents and, where required, group existing billing documents into an invoice list for the customer.

control_plane.why: decide which references can share one billing document
decide which billing documents are grouped for presentation/settlement
provide common header values required for convergence

impact_summary: Physical fulfillment remains unchanged; the process changes document granularity, customer settlement and billing operations.
constraints: Collective billing and invoice lists are not the same: the first merges reference documents into invoices, the second groups already-created billing documents.
Unexpected header differences create billing splits that users often discover only after staring accusingly at the due list.
lead_questions: Are we consolidating deliveries into one invoice or invoices into one invoice list?
Which exact field causes an unwanted billing split?
Does customer accounting require one legal invoice or only one statement-style grouping?

processes.title: Sales Rebate Processing
processes.memory_hook: The price is not finished at invoice time.
processes.business_intent: Manage retrospective customer rebates and bonus agreements using condition contracts, business-volume determination, accruals and periodic/final settlement.

control_plane.why: defines partner, validity, eligible business volume and rebate conditions
decides which transactions contribute to the agreement
control accrual and payment timing

data_hinges.changes: which billed sales count toward rebate

impact_summary: A sale that was commercially complete at invoice time can still create later liabilities, credits and margin adjustments.
constraints: Settlement Management is broader than classic SD pricing; ownership spans pricing, billing, accounting and contract governance.
Incorrect business-volume criteria can create financially large errors long after the original invoices were posted.
lead_questions: What business volume counts and why?
When is an accrual required?
How do returns and credit memos reduce eligible rebate volume?
Who owns settlement exceptions?

processes.title: Sales Payment Overlays
processes.memory_hook: Same sales flow, different way of proving the customer can pay.
processes.business_intent: Overlay the sales process with payment-instrument or payment-authorization logic such as SEPA direct debit mandates or digital card/payment-service processing.

control_plane.control: payment method / mandate / payment card context
control_plane.why: selects how payment is authorized or collected
connects ERP documents to external payment providers where applicable
carries payment context into receivable and clearing

impact_summary: The order-to-cash documents remain familiar, but payment risk and external integration become part of the process contract.
constraints: Payment capability is localization, provider and deployment sensitive.
Do not confuse payment authorization with credit management; they answer different risk questions.
lead_questions: Who owns payment authorization: S/4, a payment service, or commerce?
What happens when authorization succeeds but order creation fails?
How are refunds linked to the original digital payment?
